gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much energy these kit batteries actually deliver: Notebookcheck measured about 850 Wh (83%) from the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2's 1,024 Wh and OutdoorGearLab measured 890 Wh, while Notebookcheck got about 90% usable energy from EcoFlow's 1.92 kWh STREAM at 500 W and found AC charging took about 15% extra input energy.
standout_why: I read the two cited rival pages. balconysolarkits.us/kits (last verified 2026-10-02) gives no measured efficiency, standby draw or delivered output for any kit and names no tester. solutionenergy.com/solar/balcony/with-battery (updated 2026-10-03) says 'we did not test these products'. Its ~870 Wh usable figure for a 1,024 Wh station is the author's own estimate, not a measurement. The cited wattbalcon.fr page would not open (TLS certificate error), and the cited us.zendure.com page returned HTTP 429, so I could not check either. None of the pages I could read names Notebookcheck, OutdoorGearLab or Stiftung Warentest, or gives a measured delivered-Wh or charging-loss figure.
decides: It confirms the pick rather than changing it. The Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 kit, the one battery kit ChatGPT showed as available in the US, delivers about 850–890 Wh of its 1,024 Wh in two named tests, so a shopper should plan around roughly 0.85–0.9 kWh per night, not 1 kWh. The lab data on the grid-tied EcoFlow STREAM and Zendure SolarFlow 800 Pro come from EU 230 V units. Those units' US availability is limited, sold out, or a different configuration in Zendure's case. Stiftung Warentest graded three of the five balcony batteries it tested (including the STREAM Ultra and SolarFlow 800 Pro) 'Mangelhaft' for electromagnetic interference, but its per-model grades are paywalled. That is a caution to flag, not a reason to drop either one.

findings.label: Measured usable energy and charging loss
findings.value: about 90% of stored energy usable at a constant 500 W feed-in; AC charging needed about 15% extra input energy
findings.source_title: Notebookcheck: Decentralized balcony power plant system avoids 800 W limit – EcoFlow Stream in a practical test
findings.note: Marcus Schwarten, published 2025-09-23 (modified 2026-10-05). EU 230 V units. The charging-loss test used the Stream AC Pro, charged from its 13% discharge limit to 100%. Smart-meter regulation responded in 'a few seconds'. No standby draw was measured. The author suggests dynamic-tariff arbitrage needs a price spread of at least 25% to pay.

findings.source_title: Notebookcheck: Balcony power plant system with up to 11.5 kWh and AI – Zendure SolarFlow 800 Pro review & comparison
findings.note: Marcus Schwarten, published 2025-09-01. EU unit, constant 400 W discharge down to the 10% limit. 1.82 / 1.92 = 94.8%. Grid charging was at up to 1,000 W.
